title: MyISAM versus InnoDB
context: What is the difference between MyISAM and InnoDB?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): MySQL questions
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: MyISAM has no transactions, no foreign keys and table-level locking, so writes block readers of the whole table. It crashes more easily and needs repair after failures. InnoDB supports ACID transactions, row-level locking, foreign keys and crash recovery through the redo log. InnoDB has been the default since MySQL 5.5. Use InnoDB for almost all new tables.

points.title: Transactions and locks
points.why: InnoDB has transactions and row locks. MyISAM has neither.

points.title: Crash safety
points.why: InnoDB recovers from crashes using logs. MyISAM tables can need repair.
